title: Regional fallback runbook and routing matrix
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic runbook + routing matrix for regional fallback and graceful degradation. Goal: minimize end-user latency and error surface during regional capacity constraints while preserving cost and quality objectives. This doc is intentionally operational — shorter than the design proposal and includes concrete thresholds, decision rules, and a small test plan.

Context and constraints:
- We operate hosted inference across three primary regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) with dedicated pools for high-tier customers.
- Each region exposes multiple model variants per family (e.g., gptx-3-16b-fp16, gptx-3-16b-q4, gptx-3-8b-q4). Variants trade quality for latency/cost.
- Control plane runs in a replicated, leaderless mode; routing decisions are executed at the edge routing layer with policy updates propagated via config store (etcd + signed checkpoints).
- SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive products, 99.9% availability at route-level.

Key concepts (short):
- Spillover: traffic forwarded from saturated region to another region.
- Spillback: reverse flow when primary region recovers.
- Soft-degrade: reduce model quality (variant) while retaining same route and auth semantics.
- Hard-fallback: route to a lower-tier model family or cached response.
- Regional score: runtime health metric combining queue-depth, avg-latency, and error-rate (0..1, higher is healthier).

Routing decision matrix (executed per-request):
Inputs: route_id, requested_model, customer_tier, region_hint, token_budget, realtime_flags
Runtime signals: local_region_score, neighbor_scores[], model_variant_availability, kv-cache-hit
Rules (applied left-to-right):
1) If local_region_score >= 0.7 and model_variant_available -> route locally to requested_model.
2) If local_region_score in [0.5,0.7): check kv-cache-hit -> if hit serve locally; else attempt soft-degrade variant (same family, lower precision).
3) If local_region_score < 0.5: attempt spillover to neighbor region with score >= 0.7 and latency budget allows (estimated RTT + model p95 < token_budget). Prefer regions by (latency_penalty + cost_delta) ascending.
4) If no neighbor qualifies, and customer_tier == enterprise -> failover to dedicated capacity pool within region (if reserved capacity available).
5) Otherwise, serve degraded-mode model-family (smaller model) in local region if available, annotated with "degraded-mode" in response metadata.
6) If degraded model not available and cache empty -> return 503 with "retry-after" and telemetry tag 'fallback_unavailable'.

Policy examples (operational knobs):
- Circuit breaker (per region): open when GPU-queue > 95% for 90s OR sustained p95 > 500ms for 2m. Close after 10m of healthy metrics (<70% queue AND p95 < 300ms).
- Soft-degrade threshold: local_region_score < 0.7 AND cache_miss rate > 0.3 over 1m window.
- Spillover cap: do not spillover more than 20% of route qps to any single target region without explicit approval.
- Cost-aware routing flag: allow_spillover_cost_limit = 1.15 (only choose a region whose estimated per-token cost is <= 1.15x local).

Control plane mechanics:
- Policy engine: OPA-based policy bundle published to routing layer. Bundle contains: per-route allowed variants, tier-based preferences, spillover topology, and emergency overrides.
- Rollout: policy bundles are versioned and signed. Default rollout uses 10s apply window with 3s jitter to prevent synchronized reconfigs.
- Local cache sync: edge routers keep a 2s TTL key-value snapshot to avoid excessive control plane chatter.

Operational runbook (incident playbook):
Trigger: region X sends alert 'region_score < 0.5' and error-rate > 2%
1) Triage (first 5 minutes):
   - Pager oncall: check region dashboard (Console/Region X) and perf traces.
   - Run diagnostic command: curl https://origin.region-x.internal/health and check GPU queue depths via CI metrics.
   - If circuit breaker is not already open, open it manually for route-sensitive customers: PATCH /control/policy/breakers/region-x -> {open:true, reason:"manual triage"}.
2) Mitigation (5-20 minutes):
   - Enable spillover to preferred neighbor(s) with rate limit 10% per minute. API: POST /control/spillover with targets and rate.
   - For high-risk routes: enable soft-degrade for non-enterprise customers: update route policy to prefer q4 variants.
   - Notify CS slack channel and customers with dedicated capacity (if impacted).
3) Recovery (20-60 minutes):
   - Monitor region_score and queue depth. If region_score > 0.7 for 10 minutes, progressively spillback 50% of traffic, then 100% over 5 minutes.
   - Close circuit breaker after 10 minutes of stable health.
4) Postmortem actions:
   - Create incident doc and tag with JIRA INF-xxxx. Save traces and decision timestamps.
   - Add a regression test to the routing simulator for the failing scenario.

Testing and validation plan (before rollout):
- Simulation harness: create a synthetic workload with bursty arrivals. Run routing-sim with toggles (circuit-breaker thresholds, spillover caps) to measure p95 and cost impact.
- Smoke: during canary window enable spillover but with traffic shaping (1% shadow then 5% then 20%).
- Chaos: run a controlled kill of primary region worker pool and observe auto-spillover behavior in staging.

Observability signals to instrument (minimal):
- region_score time series (per region, 10s granularity)
- spillover_rate by route and target_region
- model_variant_served counts and latency distributions
- routing_decision_trace: sampled per route with decision path label (local/soft-degrade/spillover/dropped)
- customer-impact tag propagation in traces for enterprise customers

Notes on model variants strategy (policy-level):
- Variants are grouped into families and graded by a quality index (Q). Routing policies should prefer same family variants (higher Q first) to preserve semantics.
- For short-lived high-throughput traffic (completion < 200 tokens) prefer smaller but faster variants; for semantic-critical routes keep higher Q even during soft-degrade (enterprise opt-in).

Open questions and proposals to decide: 
- Should spillover topology be fully connected (every region can spill to every other) or constrained to a ring/mesh based on egress cost? (proposal: mesh with cost-aware edge pruning)
- Automatic per-customer spillover exclusions (some customers may disallow cross-region traffic for compliance). Need fine-grained policy flag.
- Fallback cache policy: how long should cached responses be considered safe before we force a model call? (proposal: route-level TTLs; default 60s for chat context-free completions)

Immediate actions for this doc:
- Get signoff from SRE and Compliance on cross-region spillover policy (owners: Marco + Priya) by 2025-02-01.
- Add routing-sim test for the 95% queue spike scenario (owner: Daniel) and run in staging by 2025-02-10.
- Draft customer communication template for enterprise customers when we enable cross-region spillover (owner: CS lead).

Notes to self / loose ends (working doc style):
- Need a short help-text for Console explaining "degraded-mode" flag semantics shown in request trace.
- Confirm whether Dedicated pools are excluded from automatic soft-degrade; current default is excluded, but some customers want opt-in soft-degrade for cost smoothing.

References and quick links:
- Design doc: CONFLUENCE-INF/Regional-Fallback-Design
- Routing sim tool: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim
- Incident runbook template: CONFLUENCE-INF/Incident-Runbook-Template
